claims.text: Learning in the formal sense is defined with respect to a target concept the learner is trying to recover, and the guarantee bounds the probability that the learned rule disagrees with that target by more than a stated amount. The existence of something to disagree with is what makes the guarantee statable at all.

source.title: L. G. Valiant, A theory of the learnable, Communications of the ACM 27(11):1134-1142, November 1984, doi 10.1145/1968.1972

claims.text: MacQueen coined the term k-means in the Proceedings of the Fifth Berkeley Symposium in 1967, pages 281 to 297, describing methods for classification and analysis of multivariate observations. The procedure partitions observations to minimise a stated within-group criterion; the number of groups is supplied rather than discovered, and the criterion is chosen by the analyst rather than given by the data.

source.title: J. MacQueen, Some methods for classification and analysis of multivariate observations, Proceedings of the Fifth Berkeley Symposium on Mathematical Statistics and Probability, pages 281-297, 1967

beats.broke: two activities get filed under the same heading — recovering a rule that maps inputs to a known answer, and finding structure where no answer exists — and they differ in whether there is anything to be wrong about
beats.fix: ask what would count as an error before choosing a method: with a target, error is measurable and a held-out estimate means something; without one, the objective you chose is the only standard available
beats.cost: in the second case the objective is the assumption, so a result cannot be validated in the sense the first case allows — it can only be checked against the criterion that produced it, or against what it is later used for
beats.interview: how you would know whether a clustering is any good
